The man-made lake, created in the past by the local Italian community and subsequently abandoned, is adjacent to the city in the Oromia region.

During the tour, Prime Minister Abiy thanked President Meloni for the concrete support and highlighted the significant impact the project has had in terms of job creation in an area with a high rate of youth unemployment.

Thanks to an investment of EUR 25 million by Italy, the lake area has been restored with the goal of transforming it into a tourism hub, linked also to the culture and tradition of coffee, a sector whose historical roots lie in this region and which strongly contributes to Ethiopian exports and employment levels.

In particular, thanks also to a dredging machine from Italy, debris and invasive flora have been removed from a 35-hectare area, increasing the lake’s surface area and improving water quality. The surrounding landscape and green urban areas have also been redeveloped, involving 19 hectares and with 3,000 new trees planted, thereby strengthening erosion control.

La tête de notre pays “est un morceau d'Europe centrale, tandis que nos pieds sont immergés dans la mer Méditerranée", a ajouté Meloni, observant que cela “fait de nous un pont naturel entre le nord et le sud de l'Europe, entre l'Europe dans son complexe, l'Afrique et du Moyen-Orient".
